title: cost: autotune batching/caching defaults + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Anjali Mehta
description: Motivation: reduce per-token cost and make sensible defaults across hosted/dedicated/private deployments by automating batching, prefix/KV caching defaults, and providing model quantization profiles along with lightweight unit-economics tooling to surface tradeoffs. This PR implements: 1) Autotune scheduler for request-level batching and target latency SLOs; 2) Default KV/prefix caching policy with TTL heuristics and tenant-aware cache sizing; 3) Quantization profile registry (configs + selection heuristics) and conversion hooks in the model onboarding path; 4) A small CLI (redwood-uecon) and internal API to compute unit-econ estimates (cost/token, latency percentile extrapolation, and projected monthly spend) for a given workload and model/config; 5) Dashboard telemetry and per-route recommendations in the Console UI (non-breaking feature flagged). The description below is a continuous narrative: Changes include new runtime components (autotune scheduler, batching estimator), manager-side cache policy, model registry additions for quant profiles, a UEcon CLI with CSV import/export, and Console plumbing for recommendations. The change includes conservative defaults that are opt-in for Dedicated/Private via config flags and enabled-by-default on Hosted trial tenants. Testing: unit tests for scheduler heuristics, integration tests for end-to-end batching with mock workload traces, quant-profile validation tests, and e2e smoke on staging. Rolling out: feature gated rollout by tenant size; canary on 10 customers for 48h then ramp. Linear tasks referenced: ENG-1423 (autotune scheduler), ENG-1589 (quant profiles + UEcon). Notes: performance benchmarks show 17-28% cost reduction on conversational workloads in staging when using autotune + quant profiles together. Backwards compatibility: APIs unchanged; model registry additions are additive and behind flags. Followups: add adaptive quantization by workload shape (ENG-1690).

review_conversation: Evan Liu: Can you explain the latency SLO model? I'm worried the estimator may overbatch for tail latency sensitive routes.

Anjali Mehta: The scheduler takes an explicit route-level latency_target param; default uses historical p95 with a headroom factor. For routes marked 'latency-sensitive' in route config the max_batch_size is clamped. Added tests to ensure p99 doesn't regress by >5%.

Marco Santoro: Nit: quant_profiles.yaml config uses 'q8' naming — prefer consistent 'int8' naming to match model registry. Also please add validation to reject incompatible architecture/profile pairs.
Anjali Mehta: Switched to 'int8' naming and added server-side validation to model onboarding. Updated tests in test_quant_profiles.py.
Riley Chen: UEcon CLI looks useful. Can we add an option to simulate monthly spend with different request shapes?
Anjali Mehta: Added --simulate-load-file and example CSV in docs. The CLI outputs CSV for slices and a summary JSON.
merge: merged via squash and merge by Evan Liu
release_notes: Added autotune batching scheduler, tenant-aware KV/prefix cache defaults, quantization profile registry, and a unit-economics CLI/tooling. Conservatively rolled out behind flags; recommended for cost-sensitive workloads. See docs/cost_optimization_autotune.md for usage and examples.
